painpoints.text: Pre-existing compile break: `cargo nextest run -p fabro-sandbox` with default features fails at lib/components/fabro-sandbox/src/lib.rs:18 — `pub use managed_labels::RUN_ID_LABEL;` lacks the `#[cfg(any(feature="docker", feature="daytona", test))]` gate its module has, so integration-test builds hit E0432. Reproduced on planner commit 1e3f7fc with changes stashed (run 01M1YJ8R820R7ZMSN55GJGMZ4A). Any tester gate that compiles fabro-sandbox without the docker feature will go red on this. Fix: move the cfg gate onto the pub use or make the module unconditional.

observations: fabro-sandbox clippy with `--features docker --all-targets -D warnings` already fails pre-existing on `large size difference between variants` in provider.rs:25 and sandbox_spec.rs:24 (Docker variants only compiled under the feature); verified identical with my change stashed — a tester running clippy this way will need to attribute these correctly.
docker.rs is entirely feature-gated, so the required clippy/fmt scope for changes there must include `--features docker`; default-feature builds never compile the file.

painpoints.text: The quality gate's clippy runs touched crates with default features, exposing a pre-existing compile break (fabro-sandbox E0432 from commit 4c1ca7e, ungated `pub use managed_labels::RUN_ID_LABEL`) only when this crate first became a touched crate — the implementing seed got blamed for a latent break it didn't cause (run 01M1YJ8R820R7ZMSN55GJGMZ4A, tester fail). Fix idea: gate could run a one-time `cargo check --all-features -p <crate>` baseline or CI could compile crates under default features on every merge so cfg-rot is caught at authoring time, not at seed time.

observations: The seed's own bug manifested live during this pass: after edit_file writes, `lib/components/fabro-sandbox/src/push_credentials.rs` had mtime 1970-01-01, so cargo check replayed stale dead-code warnings from cache instead of recompiling — diagnostics cited line numbers that no longer matched the source. `touch` on the edited files forced recompilation.
